paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: a speech can sound strong and still miss the person standing right in front of it. Bildad has big, vivid pictures: lamps going out, traps in the path, roots drying up. He closes with, "Surely such is the dwelling of the wicked and the place of one who does not know God." (Job 18:21) I've given advice with total confidence and zero information, and the dough never once thanked me.

Now remember who Bildad is talking to. He opens by telling Job, "Show some sense, and then we can talk," and calls him someone who tears himself in anger (Job 18:2, 4). But God Himself said there was no one on earth like Job, a blameless and upright man (Job 1:8). I think those words land hard on a man who is already hurting.

So here's what I'm taking out of the oven. When someone around you is suffering, don't rush to hand them a verdict, even a verdict that sounds wise. Listen first, and remember you don't see everything God sees. And Job's story is NOT over, friend, so keep your apron on.
